candidate_relations.reason: Pulmonary embolism is a different cause of dyspnea; chest CT and MRI show an intra-SVC fat mass rather than emboli.
Histiocytoma is a different tumor lineage from an interatrial septal lipoma.
Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum with SVC obstruction is the main related fat lesion but is nonencapsulated hyperplasia, not a true lipoma.
SVC syndrome due to thrombosis asserts an incompatible cause; MRI/MRA show extrinsic fat-mass compression without a bland thrombus diagnosis.
Constrictive pericarditis is a different mechanism of exercise limitation and is not supported by the described imaging.
Coronary artery disease is not the cause of the documented SVC narrowing by a fat-signal mass.
Extrinsic SVC compression captures the hemodynamic mechanism but omits the interatrial septal lipoma that is the required lesion.
Superior vena cava syndrome is the clinical manifestation of the compression, not the lipoma itself.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy is a different myocardial disease and does not explain the fat-signal SVC mass.
Mediastinal lipomatosis is related fatty infiltration but in the wrong compartment relative to an interatrial septal lipoma.
Cardiac lipoma is the correct tumor class but lacks the required interatrial septal anatomy and SVC compression.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: cardiac lipoma missing IAS and SVC

candidate_relations.reason: Hyperlipidemia-related cardiovascular disease is a comorbidity, not the intra-cardiac fat mass.
Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum is related but histologically distinct from an encapsulated interatrial lipoma.
Cardiac sarcoidosis is a different infiltrative disease and does not match the fat-signal mass.
Lymphoma is a different mediastinal mass etiology than a fat-signal interatrial lipoma.
Cardiac tumor is a parent category missing lipoma histology, interatrial location, and SVC compression.
Thyroid cancer metastasis is a plausible competing mass in this history but is incompatible with a fat-signal lipoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: metastasis vs lipoma given thyroid history

case_quality_flags: TTE reports lipomatous hypertrophy while CT/MRI describe a well-defined fat mass compressing the SVC, matching lipoma more than LHIS
